newsitem.title: INDIA: Frail Mother Teresa leaves on foreign tour.
newsitem.headline: Frail Mother Teresa leaves on foreign tour.

text.p: Mother Teresa left Calcutta en route for Rome on Thursday, saying she also hoped to visit Poland and the United States, health permitting.

"I may go to Poland and the United States of America if my health permits," the 86-year-old nun told reporters at Calcutta airport as she left for her first foreign tour since recovering from serious illness last year.
The Nobel Peace laureate, wearing her trademark blue-edged white sari, walked steadily into the airport lounge but was later taken to the aircraft in a wheelchair.
"I am feeling better now. God bless you," the nun, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and dying, said cheerfully.
She was accompanied by her successor as superior-general of the Missionaries of Charity, Sister Nirmala, four other nuns and her doctor, Patricia Aubanel.
"Mother is very happy, and anxious to go to Rome. She'd like to travel to other places but it is not yet decided. It will be decided on the basis of her health conditions," Aubanel said.
"One of the purposes of Mother Teresa's visit to Rome is to formally introduce Sister Nirmala to Pope John Paul," she said.

Sister Nirmala took over as the head of the Calcutta-based Missionaries of Charity in March. Mother Teresa stepped down after being admitted to hospital three times last year for heart surgery and emergency care.
Aubanel, who was part of the team that carried out Mother Teresa's three heart operations in 1991, 1993 and 1996, said on Wednesday she had advised the nun to visit only Rome.

The nuns, who were scheduled to break journey in New Delhi for a few hours before leaving for Rome on Thursday night, were also carrying four babies to Europe for adoption, a Missionaries of Charity spokeswoman said.
Mother Teresa's recent tours outside India have been marred by ill health.
On a visit to Europe in 1993, she injured three ribs in a fall. On a trip to the United States in 1991, she fell ill midway through the visit and had to undergo the first of her heart operations.
